findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() — I/O failure panics on missing/unreadable file
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and map fs::read_to_string errors via map_err or ?

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() — parse failure panics on non-numeric input
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV row (e.g. name,"not_a_number") panics the caller instead of returning a typed ParseError
findings.fix: use map_err on parse to return a typed error like ParseError::InvalidValue, and return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>

findings.problem: as u16 lossy cast from u32 — values above 65535 silently truncate
findings.failure_mode: a value like 70000 wraps to 4464 silently, corrupting data with no error
findings.fix: use try_into() -> Result<u16, TryFromIntError> and map to a typed Overflow error, or validate range with a checked bound

findings.problem: Unbounded collect into Vec<String> from arbitrary file — no size cap on input lines or field count
findings.failure_mode: an attacker or misconfigured file with millions of lines causes OOM or denial of service
findings.fix: enforce a MAX_LINES domain cap, use try_reserve with checked capacity arithmetic, and map allocation failure to a typed error

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) — hidden I/O side effect inside a function that claims to load frames
findings.failure_mode: the function has a hidden logging side effect that cannot be suppressed in benchmarks or tests, and leaks shell concerns into what should be a data-loading pipeline
findings.fix: remove println entirely; pass an optional logging callback in the shell layer, or return a count/metadata field on Record if tracking is needed

findings.problem: parts[0] — unchecked indexing into split result
findings.failure_mode: a line with zero commas (e.g. "single_field") panics via index out of bounds
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and match on the two-option result, returning a typed MalformedLine error when parts are missing

findings.problem: parts[1] — unchecked indexing into split result
findings.failure_mode: a line with one comma but no second field (e.g. "name,") panics via index out of bounds
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and match on the two-option result, returning a typed MalformedLine error when the value part is missing

findings.problem: Record uses raw String and u16 — no newtypes, no smart constructor, no domain invariants
findings.failure_mode: any caller can construct Record { name: "".into(), value: 0 } with invalid data; the domain has no type-level guarantee that name is non-empty or value is in a valid range
findings.fix: introduce a non-empty string newtype (e.g. Name), a validated Value or u16 with smart constructor, and a private-constructor Record with a static new() that returns Result

findings.problem: load_frames mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string), parsing (split/trim), side effects (println), and collection (collect into Vec) in a single unresult function
findings.failure_mode: no caller can use any layer of this pipeline independently; every invocation triggers file read, logging, allocation, and potential panics
findings.fix: split into: shell function load_frames(path) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> that handles I/O, and a pure parse_lines(impl Iterator<Item=&str>) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> for the core logic

findings.problem: load_frames accepts &str path with no validation — any string reaches fs::read_to_string
findings.failure_mode: path traversal (e.g. /etc/shadow), empty string, or null bytes reach the filesystem layer with no guard
findings.fix: validate path is non-empty, reject path traversal components, or use a Path-based type with a smart constructor that validates the input

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_frames throughput or latency
no profiler evidence for allocation hot path in the parsing pipeline
no allocation budget documented for the collect::<Vec<String>> step
no command evidence for benchmark or profiler runs
no second-ring evidence for zero-cost or performance claims
residual_risk: Static review only. The crate compiles but contains 10 BLOCKER findings: unwrap on I/O and parse, lossy as cast, unchecked indexing, hidden println I/O, unbounded allocation, no domain types, no Result return, no input validation, and no benchmark/profiler evidence. The function as written will panic on any malformed input, missing file, or value exceeding 65535. All panics are production-blockers under Holzman doctrine.
